anomalies.observed: On page 2, U1 (LM1117-5.0) has its input pin 3 (VI) and its output pin 2 (VO) both tied to the same +5V net (two +5V arrows, with C2 on the VI side). The VCC rail (the higher fan rail used at JP1/R6/C1) is not connected to U1 at all.
anomalies.expected: A fixed-5 V linear regulator must have a higher-voltage input than its output. The intended topology is VCC (the fan rail, which is >5 V as implied by the 5V1 clamp D1 on the TACH pull-up R6) feeding U1.3, with U1.2 producing the +5V rail that powers U2/U3. As drawn the regulator's VIN and VOUT are shorted together, so it is bypassed and cannot generate +5V.

evidence.quote: Page 2: U1 LM1117-5.0, pin3 VI -> '+5V', pin2 VO -> '+5V', pin1 GND -> GND; C2 100nF on VI side.
Page 1: VCC net appears at R6 (TACH pull-up), C1 and JP1 pin2; +5V net appears at U2/U3 VCC pins — two distinct rails.

anomalies.impact: The 5 V MCU supply is not derived from the board's main (VCC) rail; the regulator does nothing. The ATtinys only power up when +5V is injected externally via J1/J4, and the VCC-to-+5V regulation path is broken.

anomalies.observed: On page 1 the wire leaving J3 pin 2 (labelled POT) continues to the node at the bottom of C3, and that same node also carries an 'RST' (active-low) label. Because RST is also on J1.4, J4.5 and U2.1/U3.1, this merges the potentiometer signal with the reset net.
anomalies.expected: POT (the ADC speed-set input on U2.2/U3.2) and RST (U2.1/U3.1, also the ISP reset on J4.5 and J1.4) must be separate nets. RST should be a proper active-low reset line (pull-up/RC), not driven by the pot wiper.

evidence.quote: Page 1: J3 pin2 'POT' wire runs right into C3 bottom, which is also labelled 'RST' (overbar).
Page 1/2: 'RST' also on J1.4, J4.5, U2.1, U3.1; 'POT' also on U2.2, U3.2.

anomalies.impact: The MCU reset pin is driven by the potentiometer; turning the pot toward ground holds both ATtinys in reset, and the ISP header cannot take the chip out of reset reliably. The pot's ADC reading is also corrupted by the reset pin's internal pull-up.

parsed.summary: Two connectivity deviations are visible: U1 (LM1117-5.0) has VIN and VOUT both tied to +5V (regulator bypassed, VCC never regulated to +5V), and the POT net is bridged onto the active-low RST net via the C3 node. Both would make the board behave differently from the intended ATtiny fan controller.
